children: Our Political Bureau New Delhi: Ahead of the CJP protest, Delhi Police on Friday held a high-level meeting at its headquarters. Senior officers are reviewing the emerging law-and-order situation ahead of the protest. Police will also discuss and examine the recent observations made by the Supreme Court. According to Delhi Police sources, senior officers are assessing the emerging situation and discussing the observations made by the Supreme Court regarding restrictions imposed in the national capital ahead of the proposed demonstration.

Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) is in force in the New Delhi area, and police have warned that violations of the restrictions could invite legal action. Delhi Police has denied permission for the Cockroach Janata Party's (CJP) October 10 demonstration at Jantar Mantar, citing short notice and alleged non-compliance during an earlier protest.

Joint Commissioner of Police Nupur Prasad said the application was submitted on October 7, against the requirement of at least 10 days' advance notice. Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita remains in force across the New Delhi district, police said.

Authorities have also ordered a 24-hour internet shutdown within a 4-km radius of Jantar Mantar ahead of the protest. The suspension will remain in effect from 10 pm on October 9 to 10 pm on October 10, covering the area around the Janpath-Kartavya Path crossing. Airtel, Jio, Vodafone-Idea and MTNL have been directed to implement the order. Authorities have deployed around 25,000 police and paramilitary personnel, with more than 120 companies of Central Armed Police Forces expected to assist in security arrangements.

Delhi Metro restrictions had included closing entry and exit gates at 57 stations from 9 pm on Friday. Several Mail, Express, MEMU and EMU trains scheduled around New Delhi and Hazrat Nizamuddin between 4 am and 2 pm on Saturday have also been cancelled amid anticipated traffic congestion.

Delhi has ordered retail liquor shops to remain closed on October 9 and 10.
